verification.note: addons/intelligence/app/workers/frame_ocr.py:166-177 defines module-level `_normalised_quad(quad, width, height)`. It returns None for non-positive dimensions, for a quad that is not 8 points, or for a non-finite quad. Otherwise it divides x by width and y by height, clamps to [0,1] and rounds to 4 places. Its only call site is frame_ocr.py:454-456 inside `_read_video`. `_read_video` also now binds `ocr_image = _ocr_image(image)` (line 426) and passes it to `_read_boxes` (line 427), so `ocr_image.size` (line 447) can serve as the normalisation base. `_read_boxes` (line 262) is not touched at that call site. The touch-point list in docs/specs/frame-ocr-line-boxes.md:236-246 does not name `_normalised_quad`. The helper only serves `_read_video`'s recording of quads, so this is a scope note and not a behavioural defect. I could not view the diff itself because I have no git access. That the helper is new is inferred from its absence in the spec and in the touch points.

In tests/test_spec_addon_133_frame_ocr_reread_text.py, line 1 (module docstring: 'a stored read writes the current rule'), line 104 (section comment), line 108 (`test_spec_addon_133_i6_a_first_read_is_stored_under_the_current_rule`) and line 260 (`..._keeps_its_frames_under_the_current_rule`) use 'current rule' wording. In tests/test_spec_addon_133_loft_read_rule.py, lines 1-2 (docstring) and line 28 (`test_spec_addon_133_section_3_a_loft_read_is_stored_under_the_current_rule`) do the same. Earlier names used 'rule two': docs/process/reviews/feature-frame-ocr-read-interval/mutation-review.md:27 cites `test_..._i6_a_first_read_is_stored_under_rule_two`. docs/specs/frame-ocr-line-boxes.md:253-258 allows 'rule two' → 'current rule' renames only for the three named files (outdated, reread, worker_reread). For other files, the only allowed change is the 2→3 expectation. So renaming in these two files goes beyond the listed touch points. The renames are cosmetic and keep the assertions' meaning.
